findings.message: This host did not provide a verified exact author model for the planning review.

I found no blocking errors. The 12 scenario blocks compile to 17 cases (R1: 4, R2: 6, R3: 2, R4: 4, R5: 1), which matches the Work Log. Every outcome sits under the Rule it proves. All scenarios use the real Safeword CLI entry point, and the feature tag @surface.safeword-cli resolves in surfaces.md. The Safeword Maintainer persona resolves in personas.md. Ticket out_of_scope can be read, and no scenario crosses into certification, closing, shared gates, historical repair, paid or live runs, or host/cloud recovery. The project and milestone non-goals in spec.md are also respected. The ticket declares no parent, so there are no inherited boundaries to check. Rejection scenarios are paired with positive siblings: the @demo success, and the two R4 rows that keep currency, which act as an authentic-verification control for the R3 tamper refusal. That means a constant implementation cannot pass the set. Remaining gaps are non-blocking: the @demo scenario only partly shows its Payoff, the demo's word "verifiable" is never exercised, and two R1/R3 invariants with distinct user-visible outcomes are proved only by named lower-level matrices.

Killer Demo proof is partial. The Payoff says one observation produces verifiable evidence 'while the historical ledger remains visibly unfinished and no completion authority is granted'. The @demo scenario 'Complete fixed-lane execution produces verifiable current evidence' only covers the evidence half. The ledger and authority half is proved separately in the R5 scenario, so the Rule is covered and this is not a must-fix. Either add a Then to the @demo scenario saying the result carries no completion authority and the 33 deferred identities stay unverified, or move @demo to a scenario that shows both halves.

In the @demo scenario, 'verifiable' and 'the retained full report supports every declared required assertion' are weak claims. No step in that scenario runs verification, and 'supports' is not a measurable result. Positive verification is only implied by the R4 rows whose Given starts from 'a successful observation'. Suggestion: make the Then say the report records a passing result for each of the 37 mapped cases' required assertions. Also consider saying that verifying the new observation reports current success, so success-path verification is proved in this scenario and not only assumed in a Given.

R1 requires that a changed accepted scope be refused before execution, with a recovery that differs from the dirty-input case: review an updated shipped contract, not commit or clean. Only the lower-level matrix observer-source-identity covers this before-execution refusal. The R4 outline covers the same change only at verification time. dimensions.md names the lower-level proof, so this does not block. But the user-visible recovery is distinct, so consider adding an acceptance row or scenario so the CLI wiring for this refusal is proved end-to-end.

R3 requires that an interrupted or incompletely saved attempt can never become a successful observation. In 'Retrying an interrupted attempt preserves the failed evidence', the Given already sets up an interrupted attempt with no success, so no acceptance scenario shows that interrupting a run through the CLI produces a failed, retained attempt. The lower-level matrix observer-persistence is named as the proof. Note that a same-process fault injection cannot prove the record stays correct after a real process interruption. Make sure the implementation plan includes a subprocess-level interruption check.

The R2 Scenario Outline is coherent. Its three rows (absent from the report, skipped, failed) vary only the outcome of the required assertion and share one outcome shape. Duplicate, ambiguous and unrelated-skip cases are correctly placed in the lower-level matrix observer-required-assertions.

The R4 Scenario Outline correctly pairs two semantic changes that make evidence stale (assertion source, accepted scope) with two bookkeeping or audit-only controls that keep it current. This blocks both a 'hash the whole ticket' implementation and an 'exempt the whole ticket' implementation. Each row also asserts that the retained evidence stays readable.
The mid-run candidate-change scenario uses a controlled pause rather than timing. That keeps it deterministic while covering R1's rule that the candidate is bound when the request starts.
